title: Netherlands: Generatietoets and Kinderrechtentoets
executive_summary: The Netherlands is one of two countries GYC classifies as having an enacted national Intergenerational Impact Assessment — but the instrument is administrative, not a veto. The Beleidskompas generatietoets asks ministries to test irreversible or redistributive effects on current and future generations before a decision; nobody can stall a dossier for a missing toets. A cousin tool, the Kinderrechtentoets, is a living-child CRIA now instructed for jeugdzorg bills. Bite is thin: Miljoenennota 2026 skipped the Senate's generatietoets motion; the only documented amendment is two consultation-stage safeguards on Wet reikwijdte Jeugdwet. Next public test is Prinsjesdag 15 September 2026.

layers.label: Administrative IIA (enacted method)
layers.instrument: Beleidskompas step 4 + Leidraad Toekomstgericht Beleid generatietoets
layers.role: Ministries should run a generatietoets when effects may redistribute across generations, are irreversible, or lock later cohorts in. Hulpmiddel, not a statutory veto.

layers.label: Child-rights cousin (youth-care bills)
layers.role: Four-step CRC assessment on future jeugdzorg bills, recorded in the memorie van toelichting. Kinderombudsman advises; cannot void a bill.

layers.label: Climate duty (not IIA review)
layers.instrument: Urgenda (Hoge Raad 2019) via ECHR Arts. 2 and 8
layers.role: Intergenerational climate duty of care. Does not require a pre-decision generatietoets and does not review a missing one.

constitutional_reform.significance: Unlike Italy Art. 9 or Germany Art. 20a, the Grondwet does not name future generations. Dutch IIA is method, not constitutional operationalisation.

articles.text_en: There is no Grondwet paragraph equivalent to Italy's Article 9 third paragraph or Germany's Article 20a. Intergenerational claims have been litigated through the ECHR as applied by the Hoge Raad in Urgenda.

what_lacks: No statutory veto or Council-of-State stall for a missing generatietoets
Kinderrechtentoets is not a general-statute duty — youth-care bills only

jurisprudence.overview: Dutch 'case law' for IIA is mostly administrative bite: completed toets versus changed decision. Constitutional climate doctrine (Urgenda) sits beside the tools and does not police them.

streams.label: Budget and generatietoets
streams.summary: Senate motion 36.800 D instructed a generatietoets on the Miljoenennota. MN 2026 skipped it. NPCE 2023–2030 is the only public completed toets and issued recommendations only.

key_cases.subject: Eerste Kamer motion 36.800 D versus published MN 2026 bundle
key_cases.holding_en: The motion was adopted; the 16 September 2025 Prinsjesdag bundle did not include a generatietoets annex. Completing the political instruction is still open for MN 2027.
key_cases.significance: Documented skip of the flagship national IIA on the budget. Next test 15 September 2026.

key_cases.subject: National Circular Economy Programme — nine themes × four living age bands
key_cases.holding_en: Contractor Sira Consulting completed the second v1 pilot. Recommendations issued. No primary evidence an NPCE measure was rewritten.
key_cases.significance: Worked example of the method; bite = none found.

streams.label: Kinderrechtentoets on youth-care bills
streams.summary: The only documented Dutch IIA-family amendment is consultation-stage, not enacted law. A claimed second toets on jeugdbescherming is unverified.

key_cases.subject: Two safeguards added after youth conversations
key_cases.holding_en: Immediate additional jeugdhulp when necessary; usual-care test must allow help where parents cannot provide it. Bill not yet a statute.
key_cases.significance: Only proven Dutch IIA-family rewrite — and it is still consultation text.

key_cases.subject: Minister Sterk claimed a Kinderrechtentoets; public consultation MvT has none
key_cases.holding_en: Consultation MvT (internetconsultatie document 13475) has no Kinderrechtentoets section — only §4.4 CRC framing. Post-consultation MvT was at the Raad van State as of 30 June 2026 (kst 31839-1180) and unpublished.
key_cases.significance: Do not treat the ministerial claim as a completed toets until the Tweede Kamer MvT is public.

operational_tests.test: Run after a generatiescan when effects may redistribute across generations, are irreversible, or lock later cohorts into costly-to-reverse choices. Not required on every file.
A completed toets that leaves the decision unchanged is a skip or none-found, not success. Only a recorded change to the draft counts as amendment.
Living children as CRC rights-holders on jeugdzorg bills. Not an unborn-cohort test and not a general RIA duty.

vig_framework.english_name: Generation test inside the national policy compass
vig_framework.statutory_principle: Nobody can block. Missing a toets does not void a bill or budget. Political pressure exists via the Eerste Kamer.
vig_framework.definition: A four-step assessment (scope; inventory; normative frames and futures; verification and reporting) of effects on current and future generations, documented for Beleidskompas step 5 and for beslisnota / memorie van toelichting.
vig_framework.integration: Beleidskompas step 4 (consequences), optional alongside Toekomst aan Tafel.
vig_framework.trigger: Strongly advised / necessary if effects may (a) redistribute burdens and benefits across generations, (b) be irreversible or lock future generations in, or (c) involve high uncertainty on high-impact long-term policy.
exclusions: NPCE v1 scored living age bands (<20, 20–45, 45–67, 67+), not the unborn as a legal person

institutions.name: Sponsoring-ministry policy officials
institutions.role: Write the toets using Beleidskompas / Leidraad Toekomstgericht Beleid (BZK-authored; hosted by KCBR).

institutions.name: Kinderombudsman

recommendations.text: Treat Prinsjesdag 15 September 2026 as the next generatietoets test — do not clone MN 2026.
Wait for the Tweede Kamer MvT before counting a Kinderrechtentoets on jeugdbescherming.
Do not confuse Raad van State intergenerational-justice advice (16 April 2026) with a completed generatietoets.
Keep generatietoets (future cohorts / irreversible effects) distinct from Kinderrechtentoets (living children / CRC).

local_practice.detail: Only public completed generatietoets. Four living age bands; short term to 10 years; long term from 30 years. Recommendations, not rewrites.

comparative_notes.contrast: Italy has constitutional Art. 9 plus statutory VIG in AIR — but implementing DPCMs are unpublished, so the flagship is not operating. The Netherlands has an operating method and a budget skip.
JoKER can stall a missing report at the Council of State. The Dutch generatietoets cannot.
Jugend-Check is independent and published at volume (490/91) but assesses ages 12–27, not future unborn cohorts. Dutch generatietoets is the closer future-generations tool.

litigation_track.relevance: Climate duty of care via ECHR; not IIA procedure.
